A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pKa of an ionizable base centrally located in a short model oligonucelotide can be determined by the UV absorption technique.
the deprotonation pKa value of guanine is increased in the central position of a short model oligonucletide by 2.2 units, as compared to that of the isolated mononucleotide.
the pKa values for the deprotonable groups of nucleobases in oligonucleotidic sequences depend on the sequence, the oligonucleotidal length, the temperature, and the solvent composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

pKa values of ionizable bases in nucleic acids can be significantly affected by the sequence and the physical environment, and that the acidity of a base can be tuned by changing the surrounding nucleotides.

the pKa values of deprotonable base residues in short model oligodeoxyribonuclotides can be predicted with a reasonable degree of accuracy from the sequence, the length of the oligonucleotidic strand, and the ionic strength of the solution.
, for the oligonucleotidic sequence studied, the deprotonation pKa values of guanine are not affected by the presence of the internucleotide phosphates.
